sheets.title: Qutb Shahis of Golconda (1518 – 1687)
sheets.intro: Eight Golconda sultans, Hyderabad, Telugu patronage, Mughal squeeze, Asaf Jahis.

keys.name: Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk

rows.v: 1518 – 1543; "Bade Malik"
Bahmani tarafdar (governor) of Telangana; title Qutb-ul-Mulk = "pillar of the realm"
Turkoman, born in Persia; Shia
Golconda – Golla Konda (shepherd's hill); Kakatiya mud fort, ceded by Kapaya to Bahmanis; rebuilt in granite
Murdered 1543 at son Jamsheed's instigation

traps: Bahmanis split into five Deccan sultanates

rows.v: 1543 – 50; Ibrahim fled to Vijayanagara
1550; child king, soon replaced
8 sultans over 169 years
About 7 years at Vijayanagara under Rama Raya – learnt Telugu
First to take the title "Sultan"
Malkibharam (Ibharama Chakravarti)
Ponnaganti Telaganarya – Yayaticharitra (achcha Telugu); Addanki Gangadhara – Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu; Kandukuri Rudrakavi – Nirankusopakhyanamu
Hussain Sagar (Ibrahim Cheruvu) 1562 by Hussain Shah Wali; Purana Pul over Musi 1578
Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) 1565 – Deccan league vs Vijayanagara

keys.name: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah

rows.v: Hyderabad 1591 – first Bhagyanagar; legend of Bhagmati (Hyder Mahal); planned by Peshwa Mir Momin Astarabadi
1591; four arches, four 56 m minarets; trad. end of a plague
Badshahi Ashurkhana 1594 (Muharram); Char Kaman 1592; Makkah Masjid begun (finished under Aurangzeb)
Kulliyat – earliest Urdu / Deccani diwan; pen-name "Ma'ani"; also Persian, Telugu
Mulla Wajhi – Qutb Mushtari (1609)

traps: Muhammad Quli (5th) ≠ Sultan Muhammad (6th) ≠ Sultan Quli (founder)

rows.v: Muhammad Quli's nephew and son-in-law
Dutch (1605) and English (1611) factories at Masulipatnam

keys.name: Abdullah Qutb Shah

rows.v: 1632 – English trade from Golconda ports for a fixed yearly sum
1636 – Shah Jahan's overlord; khutba in his name; tribute
Persian diamond magnate, wazir; defected to Mughals; Koh-i-Noor to Shah Jahan (trad.)
Aurangzeb (viceroy); indemnity and a daughter in marriage
Wajhi – Sabras (1635, Dakhini prose); Ghawwasi – Saif-ul-Muluk
1671, Mir Musa Khan

traps: Deed 1636 with Shah Jahan; annexation 1687 by Aurangzeb

rows.v: Brahmin brothers Madanna and Akkanna – killed
Kancherla Gopanna, their nephew; tahsildar; Bhadrachalam Rama temple; keertanas
1687 – Aurangzeb, ~8 months; Abdullah Khan Pani opened a gate; Abdur Razzaq Lari fought on; Fateh Darwaza
Prison at Daulatabad; died 1699

keys.name: Golconda economy and monuments

rows.v: Kollur mine (Krishna valley) – Koh-i-Noor, Hope; Tavernier visited
Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam); chintz, kalamkari
Acoustics (clap heard at top), water system, granaries
Ibrahim Bagh necropolis; restored by Aga Khan Trust
Fort, tombs, Charminar – tentative list 2010 only
Persian + Deccani Urdu + Telugu

traps: Golconda only on tentative list; Hampi 1986, Ramappa 2021 inscribed

keys.name: After Golconda: Mughals and Asaf Jahis

rows.v: Mughal annexation
Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I (Mir Qamaruddin Khan) founds Asaf Jahi dynasty
Seven Nizams to 1948
Hyderabad joined India 1948
